sections.h2: What is Rabun County, Georgia like for property owners?
sections.html:
Rabun County is the most sparsely settled of the four counties in this Census comparison, and its tax commissioner's office is in Clayton. The Census Bureau estimates 17,764 residents for July 2025, up 5.2% from the 2020 base of 16,886.

It covers 370.13 square miles of land, the most of the four counties compared, yet holds only 45.6 people per square mile. An unusual 31.5% of residents are 65 or older, and 52.0% of people over 16 are in the labor force, the lowest share in the comparison. Commutes are short: mean travel time to work is 23.1 minutes.

The retail numbers stand out. Retail sales in 2022 reached $448,203,000, or $25,957 per resident, and accommodation and food services sales were $92,981,000. Those figures are far above the other three counties' per-resident retail totals, which is worth knowing when you compare your house against sales elsewhere in Georgia.

sections.h2: What do Rabun County home values look like?
sections.html:
Rabun's median owner-occupied home value is $295,200 for 2020-2024, second only to Pike among the four counties, while median household income is $67,493.

Compare housing units with households: 12,695 units for 7,615 households. That wide spread means many Rabun properties are not anyone's main home. If one of those is yours, the property may not carry a homestead exemption, which affects the tax bill a buyer inherits.

sections.h2: Where do I go for Rabun County property tax questions?
sections.html:
The Rabun County tax commissioner works from 19 Jo Dotson Circle, Suite 101, Clayton, GA 30525, and the phone is (706) 782-3613. Hours are 8:00 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays, excluding major holidays.

  • Tax Commissioner: bills, collects and accepts mailed payments made out to the Rabun County Tax Commissioner.
  • Tax Assessor: sets value, takes returns between January 1 and April 1 and runs the special assessment programs.
  • Board of Equalization: hears appeals the assessors do not resolve.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: keeps deeds in the courthouse deed room.

Online payment accepts several card brands and eChecks, and the site charges a convenience fee, a 2.50% or $1.25 minimum on cards and $1.50 per eCheck. Several bills can go into one transaction using the shopping cart.

sections.h2: When are Rabun County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Taxes on real estate and business personal property are due December 1. Both the county's tax commissioner FAQ and the tax commissioner's own site give that date, although Georgia's default is December 20.

Once the due date passes, interest is added each month at the prime rate plus 3%, and a 5% penalty arrives after 120 days. If bills stay unpaid, the tax commissioner can levy on the property. A FIFA lien is recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court when taxes stay unpaid more than 90 days, and credit bureaus can see it.

Mailed payments are accepted with a United States Postal Service postmark, though a metered postmark is not. Mobile and manufactured home bills go out in January, and the tax site says they are due April 1, a date the county's other FAQ page lists differently, so confirm with the office at (706) 782-3613 before paying one.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Rabun County assessment?
sections.html:
File in writing within 45 days of the assessment notice. The Rabun assessor's FAQ states plainly that late appeals are invalid.

An appeal can rest on one of three grounds: whether the property is taxable or exempt, whether its value matches similar properties, or whether the value is too high or too low. The Board of Tax Assessors reviews it first, then the Board of Equalization hears it if no change is made. After that, either the taxpayer or the assessor can go on to Rabun County Superior Court.

The assessor's page reminds owners that the board does not create values. Assessors read the market using the cost, market and income approaches, and a sale price on a comparable nearby house is the most useful evidence you can bring.

sections.h2: Which Rabun County programs can reduce the assessment?
sections.html:
Homestead is the standard route for a primary residence. Own and occupy the home as of January 1 and apply at the assessor's office. The tax commissioner's site says an application must be received before April 1 to count that year, and the assessor's page lists a different in-person window, so call (706) 782-3613 to confirm which applies to you.

  • Preferential agricultural: assessed at 75 percent of the assessment of other property, which means 30 percent of fair market value, with a 10-year covenant.
  • Conservation use: assessed at current use value, with a 10-year covenant.
  • Environmentally sensitive: current use value for land kept in its natural condition under Department of Natural Resources rules.
  • Residential transitional: current use value where an area is shifting away from residential use.

Apply for the covenant programs between January 2 and April 1. Owners aged 62 can apply for an additional homestead exemption, and standing timber is taxed only when sold or harvested, at 100% of fair market value.

sections.h2: How does Rabun County calculate a tax bill?
sections.html:
The assessors set fair market value as of January 1, and the tax applies to 40% of it. Any exemption comes off first, then the Board of Commissioners' and Board of Education's millage rate is applied, with one mill equal to $1 per $1,000 of assessed value.

Property tax pays for police and fire services, education, roads, bridges, water, parks and other county services. Returns are filed with the assessor's office from January 1 to April 1, and taxes are charged to the owner on January 1 or to the property itself if the owner is unknown.

The state's Homeowner Tax Relief Grant credit was unfunded for the 2009 tax year, according to the county's FAQ, so check your own bill for any credit line. The tax commissioner's site also reminds owners that bills are mailed to the owner of record, not the mortgage company, and that a copy has to reach an escrow lender.

sections.h2: Can I sell my Rabun County house with a tax balance?
sections.html:
Yes. The balance is a payoff item at closing, and the first step is a call to the tax commissioner.

  1. Ask for the exact amount due, including interest and any 5% penalty.
  2. Ask whether a FIFA has been recorded.
  3. Check whether any covenant, such as conservation use, is in place, since a covenant lasts 10 years and a buyer should know about it.
  4. Have the closing attorney deduct each payoff from your proceeds.

If repairs or a long-vacant house are slowing a regular listing, a cash buyer who accepts the property as-is can close on a date you pick and take care of the tax payoff at the table.

faqs.q: When are Rabun County taxes due?
faqs.a: December 1 for real estate and business personal property. The tax commissioner's site and the county FAQ both give that date.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Rabun County property tax in person?
faqs.a: At 19 Jo Dotson Circle, Suite 101, in Clayton, weekdays from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. The phone number is (706) 782-3613.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal in Rabun County?
faqs.a: 45 days from the date of the assessment notice, in writing. The assessor's FAQ says late appeals are invalid.

faqs.q: Does Rabun County offer a farm or forest assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. Agricultural, conservation use, environmentally sensitive and residential transitional programs exist, each with a 10-year covenant, and applications run January 2 to April 1.

faqs.q: What fee applies to paying Rabun property tax by card?
faqs.a: The tax commissioner's site lists a convenience fee of 2.50% or $1.25 minimum on cards and $1.50 per eCheck.
